title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Deployment & Performance!

questions.question: What command creates an optimized production build of a Next.js app?
questions.explanation: `npm run build` (which runs `next build`) compiles and optimizes the app for production.

questions.question: In the build output, a lambda symbol (λ) next to a page means?
questions.explanation: The λ denotes a page that uses `getServerSideProps` and is rendered on each request.

questions.question: Running `npm start` starts the development server with Fast Refresh.
questions.explanation: `npm start` runs the production server; it does not include Fast Refresh or hot reload.

questions.question: Which platform is the creator of Next.js and offers zero‑config deployment?
questions.explanation: Vercel is the company behind Next.js and provides seamless Git‑based deployments with automatic optimizations.

questions.question: In Vercel, environment variables are set in the project's ______ dashboard section.
questions.explanation: You add environment variables under Project Settings → Environment Variables.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `output: 'standalone'` configuration in next.config.js?
options: To create a self‑contained build ideal for Docker deployments
questions.explanation: The standalone output mode produces a minimal production bundle without the full `node_modules`, perfect for containerized environments.

questions.question: What limitation does `next export` have?
options: Cannot use SSR, API routes, ISR, or middleware
questions.explanation: `next export` creates a purely static site. All server‑side features are unavailable.

questions.question: The tool used to keep a Node.js process alive on a VPS is called ______.
questions.explanation: PM2 is a process manager that keeps applications running and restarts them if they crash.

questions.question: What does LCP stand for in Core Web Vitals?
questions.explanation: LCP measures the time it takes for the largest visible element (hero image, heading) to render.

questions.question: How does `next/image` help with CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)?
options: By requiring `width` and `height` attributes, reserving space before the image loads
questions.explanation: Explicit dimensions allow the browser to allocate the correct amount of space, preventing content from jumping when the image loads.

questions.question: Server Components in the App Router can reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the client, improving FID/INP.
questions.explanation: Server Components render on the server and do not add to the client‑side JavaScript bundle, reducing the main thread work.

questions.question: Which hook/utility defers loading a heavy component until it's needed?
questions.explanation: `next/dynamic` is a Next.js‑specific extension of `React.lazy` that supports SSR options and custom loading components.

questions.question: In ISR with `revalidate: 60`, when does the page actually regenerate?
options: On the first request that arrives after 60 seconds since the last generation
questions.explanation: The regeneration is triggered by a user request after the revalidate interval has passed, not by a timer.

questions.question: To revalidate cached data by category, you can use `revalidateTag('posts')` inside a Server Action. Before using a tag, you must add it to a `fetch` request with the `______` option.
questions.explanation: In App Router, you tag fetch requests with `next: { tags: [...] }` so they can be purged by `revalidateTag`.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a CDN for static assets?
options: It serves content from a location geographically closer to the user, reducing latency
questions.explanation: CDNs cache assets on edge servers worldwide, so users download them from the nearest location, speeding up page loads.

questions.question: You can only deploy Next.js apps on Vercel.
questions.explanation: Next.js can run on any Node.js hosting, including Docker, AWS, Netlify, and even as a static site via `next export`.

questions.question: Which command would you use to start the production server after building?
questions.explanation: `npm start` runs the production build created by `npm run build`.

questions.question: What does the `immutable` directive in a Cache‑Control header mean?
options: The file will never be cached
The file can be stored but requires revalidation on each use
The file will not change and can be cached indefinitely without revalidation
The file is only cached on the server
questions.explanation: `immutable` tells the browser and CDN that the resource never changes, so they can skip revalidation checks entirely.

questions.question: In the Vercel deployment flow, what happens when you push to a branch linked to a project?
options: A preview deployment is automatically created for that branch
questions.explanation: Vercel creates a unique preview URL for each branch/PR, allowing you to test changes before merging.

questions.question: How does Next.js's `next/font` improve Core Web Vitals?
options: By loading fonts from Google's CDN
By self‑hosting fonts and adjusting fallback metrics to prevent layout shift (CLS)
questions.explanation: `next/font` downloads fonts at build time, serves them from your own domain, and syncs fallback font metrics, eliminating both extra network trips and layout shift.
